# Diṭṭhigata Sutta (Iti 49 (It 2.22 PTS It 43))

**ID:** Iti 49 (It 2.22 PTS It 43)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Diṭṭhigata Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Diṭṭhigata Sutta* ("Misconceptions", Iti 49; PTS It 43) is the twenty-second discourse in the second chapter (*Dukanipāta*) of the *Itivuttaka*. The discourse addresses two extreme misconceptions rooted in craving, contrasting those who hold back (*olīyanti*) due to attachment to renewed existence and those who overreach (*atidhāvanti*) into craving for annihilation; in contrast, those with direct vision see what has come to be as it is and develop dispassion toward it [Vasubandhu et al. 1991].

 DharmaNexus additionally aligns segments of the text with discourses in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 4, AN 9, AN 10), the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), the *Brahmajāla Sutta* (DN 1), the *Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga* (Vb 17), and adjacent discourses within the *Itivuttaka* (Iti 33, Iti 37, Iti 48), as well as a substantial passage (§2.1–5.4) shared with the *Visuddhimagga* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language reuse, DharmaNexus identifies machine matches between verse sections of Iti 49 and the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (Subaši manuscript) and its Tibetan version, as well as an alignment with the Tibetan *Ārya-raśmisamantamuktanirdeśasūtra* [DharmaNexus].

In modern Buddhist studies and translation, the sutta's phrasing regarding overreaching (*atidhāvanti*) is cited by Louis de La Vallée Poussin in his annotated translation of Vasubandhu's *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (Chapter 1) in connection with debates on conventions and designations [Vasubandhu et al. 1991; Detailed Outlines].
